material_findings.finding: The SLSA entry describes signature/digest/expected-field checks as directly addressing the compromised-job scenario without exposing the separate accuracy and tenant anti-forgery condition. It omits verification of the trusted builder maximum Build level and the distinction between platform-generated authentic claims and protection against a user-controlled job forging them. An honest accepted platform with weaker job isolation or tenant-controlled optional fields is distinct from compromise of the platform itself; the existing platform-compromise caveat does not express this failure boundary. The proposed matrix changes visible source/builder/parameters, but does not distinguish correct recorded claims from a job forging apparently correct claims.
material_findings.why_material: The starting threat is a compromised job falsely claiming a correct build. A digest-matching signed statement from an expected identity can contain job-controlled false data. Generic SLSA provenance plus equality checks must not be presented as addressing that threat without a bounded provenance-generation trust/accuracy condition. This is a missing mechanism failure boundary, not a requirement to deploy or certify a particular SLSA level.
material_findings.supported_scope_preserved: The listed signature, digest, predicate, source/builder/parameter checks and optional dependency recursion remain accurate. Trusted-platform compromise remains excluded. No finding asserts that L3 guarantees complete dependency evidence, hermetic builds, safe producer behavior, or a universal winning mechanism.
material_findings.disposition: Material finding retained; independent source judgment FAIL. No candidate repair or feedback.

urls_versions_and_evidence.conditions_exceptions: Authenticity, accuracy and completeness are distinct.
